final.memo:
We have seen the Company successfully transition from our venture portfolio to the public markets, and its early operating metrics are encouraging [D01, D07]. The Q3 2020 results showed 32.1% revenue growth and an improvement in operating margin to 18.7% compared to the prior-year period [D03]. This validates our initial underwriting that the platform’s AI models could differentiate credit outcomes, though we remain disciplined in monitoring this against a broader credit cycle not yet represented in training data [D03, D05].

While the stock has performed well since the IPO, rising to $62.19, this price movement reflects market sentiment and liquidity events rather than a long-term earnings inflection [D04, D07]. We recognize that the current trailing P/E of approximately 807x is a function of a small and volatile earnings denominator and is not a basis for further expansion [D04]. We are maintaining our position to observe the upcoming quarterly reports, which will provide the necessary data on loan cohorts and partner retention to confirm our thesis.

Our focus remains on the sustainability of the fee-based platform and its sensitivity to funding market conditions [D01, D05]. We will continue to evaluate the Company based on fundamental unit economics and performance against peers like Enova and LendingTree, rather than succumbing to the volatility of its early public trading days [D04, D06].
